# ECN-2026-001 Change notice - Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-HT02

Reason for change
This engineering change notice documents a formal change to the heat treat process control limits for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02). Background: recent in-process inspection findings and a review of process capability records identified excursions in quench timing that have a plausible link to surface condition variability on forged components. A cross-functional review including Production, Heat Treat, Metallurgy, Maintenance, and Quality concluded that the control of quench initiation must be clarified and enforced to reduce variability and support downstream process consistency.

Change rationale: the change establishes a firm maximum permitted quench delay to minimize microstructural divergence caused by inconsistent thermal exposure prior to quench. The change is preventive and intended to reduce rework, nonconforming product incidents, and metallurgical uncertainty. The change aligns with procedural controls in SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, and SOP-P3-L4-05 and permits a single, auditable process limit to be referenced by operators, maintenance personnel, and quality auditors.

Affected items
- Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) process control documentation and operator checklists.  
- All heat treat work orders specifying furnace EQ-P3-L4-HT02.  
- Control software alarm set points, HMI prompts, and maintenance lubrication work items that reference quench timing.  
- Training materials and operator qualification records for personnel assigned to EQ-P3-L4-HT02.

Process limit to be implemented
The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds.

Implementation
Scope and applicability: this limit applies to all parts processed in EQ-P3-L4-HT02 when the furnace is used in its normal heat treat cycles as identified in the plant routing. The limit is to be applied from the established quench initiation point defined in the furnace HMI sequence to the actual commencement of quench flow. Operators will be required to follow the updated sequence in the furnace HMI and to log events according to the revised checklist.

Steps for implementation:
- Update process documents: revise the EQ-P3-L4-HT02 process sheet and the operator checklist to include the quench delay maximum statement. Reference and update SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, and SOP-P3-L4-05 as required for consistency; changes to the SOPs will be coordinated through document control.  
- HMI and alarm configuration: configure the furnace HMI to display the quench delay target and to alarm when the elapsed time approaches the maximum. Configure the event log to capture the timestamp of quench initiation and the timestamp of quench command for audit traceability.  
- Maintenance verification: perform a mechanical and control verification to ensure the quench valve actuation and sensing are functioning to support the limit; record verification results in the equipment maintenance record.  
- Training: train all operators and maintenance staff assigned to EQ-P3-L4-HT02 on the revised process limit, HMI changes, and the requirement to log quench initiation events. Training completion will be recorded in personnel training records.  
- Verification runs: perform production verification runs using scrap or designated verification lots to demonstrate process stability under the new limit. Record outcomes, including any out-of-limit events and corrective actions, in the furnace process log.

Examples and expected responses
- Example operator response: when the HMI indicates a pending quench command, the operator verifies that the quench flow is initiated immediately. If the HMI alarm for delay is triggered, the operator follows the abnormal procedure to stop the cycle and notify Heat Treat supervision.  
- Example maintenance response: if a repeated alarm indicates inability to meet the quench delay maximum, maintenance isolates the quench valve, inspects actuators and sensors, and repairs or replaces defective components. Maintenance documents the work performed and returns the equipment to service only after a verification run is successful.

Records to keep
- Updated process sheet and operator checklist for EQ-P3-L4-HT02.  
- HMI event logs capturing quench command timestamp and quench initiation timestamp for each cycle processed in EQ-P3-L4-HT02.  
- Maintenance verification records and any corrective maintenance work orders related to quench actuation components.  
- Training completion records for all personnel assigned to EQ-P3-L4-HT02.  
- Verification run records showing process outcomes and any investigations for out-of-limit events.  
All records will be retained in the plant document control system and made available for internal audits and process reviews. The SOPs cited for procedural alignment are SOP-P3-L4-02, SOP-P3-L4-04, and SOP-P3-L4-05.

Approvals
The change requires sign-off from Heat Treat Management, Quality Engineering, Plant Operations, and Maintenance Management. Approval acknowledges review of background data, acceptance of the quench delay maximum for EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and commitment to implement the actions described under Implementation. Post-implementation, Quality Engineering will schedule a process compliance audit to review records and to validate that the change has achieved the intended reduction in process variability.

This ECN becomes effective upon completion of approvals and staged implementation as described above.
